# bpf

```go
import "github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/proc/bpf"
```

Package bpf attaches BPF programs to a control group: a device policy (cgroup\_device), an IP policy that also counts the traffic (cgroup\_skb), a bind policy (cgroup\_sock\_addr) — ADR 0215.

```
import _ "github.com/kitsunium/sdk/third-party/ebpf/cgroup" // links the backend

p, err := bpf.AttachDevice(tree.Path(), bpf.DevicePolicy{
	Default: bpf.Deny,
	Rules: []bpf.DeviceRule{
		{Type: bpf.DeviceChar, Major: 1, Minor: 3, Access: bpf.AccessAll, Verdict: bpf.Allow},
	},
})
```

### The backend is linked by an import

Loading a BPF program takes a library the standard library does not have, so the backend is the vendor module third-party/ebpf, over cilium/ebpf. A program that imports github.com/kitsunium/sdk/third-party/ebpf/cgroup — a blank import is enough — links it; any other program links nothing of cilium/ebpf, and every call here answers [NotLinked](#NotLinked). Off Linux on amd64 and arm64 the backend answers [UnsupportedPlatform](#UnsupportedPlatform); without CAP\_BPF, or on a kernel without cgroup programs, [LoadRefused](#LoadRefused). Nothing is ever a silent no-op. Call [Probe](#Probe) once, at wiring time, to learn which.

### What is refused before anything is loaded

A policy is validated first ([PolicyInvalid](#PolicyInvalid), the fields naming the rule and the field): a verdict is [Allow](#Allow) or [Deny](#Deny) and never the zero, the default included, so a policy that does not say what it decides is refused rather than read as allow-all or deny-all. The group is an absolute directory on cgroup v2 below the hierarchy's root — what a GroupTree's Path returns —; another one is [AttachFailed](#AttachFailed).

### Beside the other programs, and for how long

Every program is attached with BPF\_F\_ALLOW\_MULTI: an operation passes only when every program of the group and of its ancestors lets it through. A program stays attached until its [Program](#Program).Close, or until the group is removed: the supervisor may exit first, and its services stay under their policies.
